newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: David Jones abandons Auckland store plan.
newsitem.headline: David Jones abandons Auckland store plan.

text.p: Upmarket retailer David Jones Ltd said on Monday it would not proceed with the development of a store at Quay park Mall in Auckland, New Zealand.
The store, first announced by the company on October 31 last year, was to have been its first outside Australia and due to open some time in calendar 1999.
The company said the decision was based on continuing difficult trading conditions in Australia.

"While expansion through new stores remains one of our strategies, our immediate priority is to improve the performance of our existing stores," David Jones chief executive Peter Wilkinson said in a statement.
"We remain interested in New Zealand as a market for David Jones and will continue to monitor opportunities as they arise across the Tasman," Wilkinson said.
When it first announced the Quay Park development, David Jones said the store would be the anchor tenant and occupy 19,500 square metres of the total 60,000 square metres.
Quay Park Mall managing director Robin Sheffield said the company would now review the commencement date of the development.

David Jones said last week that its third quarter sales fell 3.2 percent to A$290.5 million, continuing a year-long trend of lower sales and weak profits which has seen investors dump the stock and led to the resignation of former chief executive Chris Tideman in early March. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
